compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
`verify.enable_code_review` (default False — src/rebar/_config_schema.py:191, parsed in src/rebar/_config_sections.py:26) is wired as an ENABLEMENT switch for the whole code-review capability, not an ENFORCEMENT switch for the gate. `gate_dispatch.code_review_enabled()` (src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py:273) is consulted at the top of `rebar.llm.code_review.shim.review_code()` (src/rebar/llm/code_review/shim.py:168), and when the flag is off a MANUAL, explicit invocation — the CLI `rebar review-code`, the library `review_code()`, the MCP `review_code` tool — does zero work and returns the inert `_disabled_review_result()` ("code-review capability disabled (verify.enable_code_review is off).", empty findings, UNPINNED provenance).

Why this is wrong:
- An explicit manual invocation IS the operator's statement of intent. Gating it on a config var conflates two different questions: "should code review run when asked?" (always yes — the user asked) and "should code review be ENFORCED as a blocking gate in automated flows?" (the thing a config knob should decide).
- AGENTS.md and `rebar explain review` tell authors to "preview the review locally with `rebar review-code` before you push". On any checkout that has not flipped `verify.enable_code_review`, that documented flow silently returns an empty PASS-looking verdict — a trap: the author believes their change was reviewed clean when nothing ran.
- The workaround inside rebar itself proves the design smell: the review-bot adapter must FORCE-ENABLE the capability to do its job (src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py:16, `request.enabled` override at gate_dispatch.py:373).
- Sibling gates already model this correctly: the criteria-registry posture distinguishes per-criterion `blocking_enabled` (src/rebar/llm/criteria/model.py:62) — i.e., enforcement — from the operation being invocable at all.

## Approach (direction, refine at claim time)
Repurpose the config axis from enablement to enforcement:
- A manual/explicit `review-code` invocation (CLI, library, MCP) always runs the four-pass gate — no config precondition beyond a working LLM config.
- The config knob (renamed or reinterpreted, e.g. `verify.enforce_code_review` / gate-posture semantics) decides only whether automated flows treat code-review as a required/blocking gate (voter posture, workflow dispatch), preserving today's off-by-default ENFORCEMENT.
- Keep the inert-empty-result shape for automated dispatch paths when enforcement is off, so existing pipelines that probe the gate cheaply do not start paying LLM costs.
- Decide the compatibility story for the existing `verify.enable_code_review` key explicitly (tombstone-warn or alias), matching the deprecation conventions used for prior config-key removals.

## File impact
- src/rebar/llm/code_review/shim.py — drop the enabled() precondition from the manual entrypoint
- src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py — split enforcement posture from invocability
- src/rebar/_config_schema.py — enforcement-semantics key (+ compat handling for enable_code_review)
- src/rebar/_config_sections.py — parse the new/renamed key
- src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py — remove the force-enable workaround
- docs/config.md — document enforcement semantics

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar review-code` on a checkout with no code-review config key set runs the four-pass gate and returns real findings (not the inert "capability disabled" result).
- [ ] The library `review_code()` and MCP `review_code` tool behave identically to the CLI in that respect.
- [ ] A config knob still exists that controls whether code review is ENFORCED as a blocking gate in automated flows, default off, and automated dispatch honors it.
- [ ] The review-bot adapter no longer needs a force-enable override to run.
- [ ] The legacy `verify.enable_code_review` key has an explicit, tested compatibility disposition (alias or tombstone-warn) consistent with prior config-key deprecations.
- [ ] docs/config.md and the `rebar explain review` guide describe the enforcement (not enablement) semantics.
compiled_state.title: Code-review config gates enablement, not enforcement: manual rebar review-code silently returns an inert empty verdict unless verify.enable_code_review is set
